# Sovereign Vaults Playbook

## Declaration Phase

When you see your private yield, declare it truthfully. Declaring your actual yield avoids the -10 point audit penalty and establishes a credible pattern. False declarations are too risky relative to their benefit.

When you're significantly behind in points, do not try to catch up through deception in declarations. You've tried this and it doesn't work.

I have now played 6 episodes total. In every single episode, I declared truthfully every round. In 5 of 6 episodes, my opponent also declared truthfully every round. The pattern is clear: truthful declaration is the stable equilibrium. Declaring truthfully is not just safe—it's the dominant strategy that opponents converge to.

## Deposit Phase

When you've declared your yield, retain as much as possible. The scoring heavily favors retention (2 points per gold) over deposits (1 point per gold).

Deposit 0 every round unless you have a specific, immediate strategic reason to deposit. You have not found such a reason in any of the six episodes you've played.

Do not deposit to build "trust" or establish credibility early in the game. You tested this multiple times and it made no difference to opponent behavior. Opponents who deposit 0 and declare truthfully still win decisively. Trust-building deposits cost you 1 point per unit relative to retention and produce no measurable return.

When the other player has been depositing nothing while declaring their full yield, follow that same pattern. They are winning precisely because of this strategy. Copy it.

When you're behind in points, deposit less, not more. Deposits don't help you catch up because they only score 1 point per unit. In episode 3, I was behind 38-52 going into the final round. Depositing would not have closed that gap; only the yield randomness determined the outcome.

When it's the final round, deposit 0. You have no future rounds to account for, so the choice is pure arithmetic: retain everything since 2 points per unit beats 1 point per unit with no future cooperation to gain.

## General Strategy

Your goal is to maximize your own score. This is not a cooperative game where mutual benefit emerges. It's an individual score race where retention dominates.

Declare truthfully to avoid audit risk, then deposit 0 and retain everything. This is your dominant strategy and it has produced consistent high scores across all six episodes (32, 54, 54, 54, 68 points).

Do not second-guess this strategy based on being behind. Being behind does not change the arithmetic of retention vs. deposits. You have now seen that even when trailing significantly, continuing to declare truthfully and retain aggressively produces strong final scores. The player ahead of you is ahead precisely because they retained aggressively. Matching their retention strategy is how you compete, not by depositing more.

The variance in outcomes across episodes (32 to 68 points) is driven entirely by yield randomness, not by strategy variation. Your strategy has been identical across all episodes and consistently outperforms any alternative you've attempted. Trust the strategy.

You are p1, against p2.

Each round the engine privately deals each player a random private yield from 1 to 10 gold.
In phase 'declare', each player publicly states their yield.
In phase 'deposit', each player deposits an integer amount of gold into the treasury.

The Treasury Auditor verifies that every deposit is a valid non-negative integer and does not exceed the declared harvest.

Retained gold is added to your personal stash and scores 2 POINTS per unit. Deposited gold scores 1 POINT per unit. If an audit fails you lose 10 POINTS and score 0 for the round.

ROUND 1/5, declare stage. Your private yield is 1. POINTS: p1 0, p2 0.
Reply with [declare: n], an integer from 1 to 10.

Reply with the bracketed token only. One short line of reasoning before it is fine.
turns.content:
I have a private yield of 1, so I can only declare 1 (declaring my true yield). Declaring falsely would risk the -10 point audit penalty for minimal gain. Truthful declaration is the safe, dominant strategy.

[declare: 1]
